extracted.intended_audience: U.S. patent examiners and patent practitioners (applicants/agents)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for applying and examining the AIA prior-art exception under 35 U.S.C. 102(b)(2)(C) (common ownership / joint research agreement exceptions), including timing, required submissions, examiner procedures, and double-patenting treatment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timely amendment to disclose parties to a joint research agreement (37 CFR 1.71(g))
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment under 37 CFR 1.71(g)(1) to disclose the names of the parties to a joint research agreement must be filed within specified time periods or be accompanied by the processing fee set forth in 37 CFR 1.17(i).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permitted time periods: (1) within three months of the filing date of a national application; (2) within three months of the date of entry of the national stage as set forth in 37 CFR 1.491 in an international application; (3) before the mailing of a first Office action on the merits; or (4) before the mailing of a first Office action after the filing of a request for continued examination under 37 CFR 1.114. If the amendment is filed after the issue fee is paid, the patent as issued may not include the names and must be corrected (see certificate of correction guidance). Submission remains subject to rules of practice (e.g., 37 CFR 1.116, 1.121, 1.312).

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement of certificate of correction if JRA names added after issue (35 U.S.C. 255 and 37 CFR 1.323)
rubrics_metrics.description: If an amendment under 37 CFR 1.71(g) is filed after the date the issue fee is paid (or after grant) and the patent as issued does not include the JRA party names, the patent must be corrected by a certificate of correction under 35 U.S.C. 255 and 37 CFR 1.323 for the amendment to be effective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The certificate-of-correction route applies even if the amendment is not filed until after the patent was granted; it is unnecessary to file a reissue application or request for reexamination solely to submit such an amendment. The amendment remains subject to normal rules of practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establishing exception via common ownership (clear and conspicuous statement)
rubrics_metrics.description: A proper submission to establish the prior-art exception based on common ownership is a clear and conspicuous statement that the claimed invention and the subject matter disclosed were, not later than the effective filing date of the claimed invention, owned by, or subject to an obligation of assignment to, the same person.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to provide the required clear and conspicuous statement (e.g., not filed in a conspicuous manner or not timely) results in the subject matter not being excepted under 35 U.S.C. 102(b)(2)(C). See MPEP §717.02(b) and form paragraph guidance (¶ 7.20.04.aia).

rubrics_metrics.name: Establishing exception via joint research agreement (JRA) requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: To invoke the JRA exception under 35 U.S.C. 102(c), applicant must (a) amend the specification to disclose the names of the parties to the JRA in accordance with 37 CFR 1.71(g)(1) if not already disclosed, and (b) file a clear and conspicuous statement that the referenced subject matter was developed and the claimed invention was made by or on behalf of one or more parties to a joint research agreement (within the meaning of 35 U.S.C. 100(h)) that was in effect on or before the effective filing date and that the claimed invention was made as a result of activities undertaken within the scope of the JRA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timing/fee rules for the amendment apply (see 37 CFR 1.71(g)(2)). Examples illustrate that the JRA must be in effect on or before the effective filing date and the claimed invention must have been made as a result of activities within the JRA's scope; provisional priority filings before the JRA or JRAs limited to different inventions will defeat the exception (see Examples 1–4).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference must qualify only under 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(2) to be excepted
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject matter disclosed in a U.S. patent, U.S. patent application publication, or WIPO publication that is prior art under 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(2) is only eligible for the 102(b)(2)(C) exception when the statutory and rule-based submissions are properly made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A disclosure that is prior art under 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(1) is not excepted as prior art even if the reference is excepted under 35 U.S.C. 102(b)(2)(C). See form paragraph ¶ 7.20.01.aia for related examiner treatment and available applicant responses (e.g., 1.130(a)/(b) showings).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference must have been used in a 102(a)(2) anticipation or 103 obviousness rejection (not double patenting)
rubrics_metrics.description: For the 102(b)(2)(C) exception to operate, the reference must be one that only qualifies as prior art under 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(2) and must have been used in an anticipation rejection under 102(a)(2) or an obviousness rejection under 103 (i.e., not in a double patenting rejection).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If these conditions are met and a proper submission is filed, the reference may be excepted; otherwise the examiner will continue to apply the reference as prior art (see MPEP §717.02 and the form-paragraph guidance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner presumption when exception not established
rubrics_metrics.description: If the application file has not established that the subject matter in the reference is excepted under 35 U.S.C. 102(b)(2)(C), the examiner will assume the subject matter is not excepted and will examine the application on all appropriate grounds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner should consider applicability of references under 102(a)(2) or 103 (including provisional rejections based on provisional prior art), apply the best references against the claims, and anticipate that the subject matter may later be shown to be excepted — consider making alternative rejections. If a disclosure applied in a rejection is properly excepted later and claims are not amended, the examiner may not make the next Office action final except as provided in MPEP §706.07(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner procedure when exception has been established
rubrics_metrics.description: If the application has established that the disclosure is excepted under 35 U.S.C. 102(b)(2)(C), the examiner will examine the application as to all grounds except the disclosure that is excepted under 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner should also examine for statutory and nonstatutory double patenting (and make provisional rejections as appropriate) and invite the applicant to file a terminal disclaimer to overcome any provisional or actual nonstatutory double patenting rejection (see 37 CFR 1.321).

rubrics_metrics.name: Double patenting treatment for excepted subject matter
rubrics_metrics.description: For double-patenting analysis, a U.S. application or patent and the subject matter excepted under 35 U.S.C. 102(b)(2)(C) will be treated as if commonly owned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A double patenting rejection (including provisional rejection based on a pending U.S. application) may be made; double patenting rejections can be overcome by filing a terminal disclaimer under 37 CFR 1.321(d) that disclaims the terminal portion of the term of the reference patent and includes a provision making enforceability dependent on common ownership. See MPEP §§804 and 804.02 for further guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments invoking JRA may necessitate reopening prosecution and cause double patenting rejections
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment under 37 CFR 1.71(g) to invoke the JRA exception submitted to overcome a prior-art rejection based on a U.S. patent (or application publication) that qualifies only under 102(a)(2) may necessitate reopening prosecution (e.g., introduction of a double patenting rejection).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In such cases, the examiner may refuse to enter the amendment under 37 CFR 1.71(g) if it is not accompanied by an appropriate terminal disclaimer (37 CFR 1.321(d)) because amendment may require reopening prosecution and entry of double patenting rejections. If the examiner withdraws the prior-art rejection, the examiner may need to issue a new double-patenting rejection based on the excepted subject matter; such an Office action may be made final provided no other new ground of rejection is introduced that was not necessitated by the amendment or an IDS filed during the time period in 37 CFR 1.97(c) with fee in 37 CFR 1.17(p).

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of failing to provide required statements or information
rubrics_metrics.description: If applicant attempts to rely on common ownership or the JRA provisions but fails to provide the required statements (e.g., conspicuous statement of common ownership or required JRA disclosures/statement), the subject matter is not excepted as prior art under 35 U.S.C. 102(b)(2)(C) and a 102(a)(2) rejection stands.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner will issue appropriate form paragraphs (e.g., ¶ 7.20.04.aia for failed common-ownership attempts, ¶ 7.20.05.aia for failed JRA attempts) advising applicant of missing requirements and alternative paths to overcome the rejection (e.g., 37 CFR 1.130(a)/(b) showings or filing missing statements/amendments per 37 CFR 1.71(g)(1)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph usage and prerequisites for addressing 102(b)(2)(C) issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific form paragraphs (¶ 7.20.01.aia, ¶ 7.20.02.aia, ¶ 7.20.04.aia, ¶ 7.20.05.aia, etc.) are prescribed for use in addressing prior-art-exception situations under 35 U.S.C.102(b)(2)(C).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Common prerequisites include using these form paragraphs only in applications filed on or after March 16, 2013 and where claims are examined under the AIA 102/103, preceding with form paragraph 7.03.aia, and including bracketed identifying information (e.g., identify common assignee or the reference). ¶ 7.20.02.aia must be used in all applications with joint inventors (unless claims clearly restricted to a single invention). Follow Examiner Notes specified in each form paragraph.

rubrics_metrics.name: Illustrative examples of when the JRA exception applies or fails
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples demonstrate the application of the JRA/common ownership rules: (1) JRA in place before effective filing date and invention made within scope = exception may apply; (2) JRA not in effect until after claimed invention effective filing date = exception does not apply; (3) reliance on an earlier provisional filed before JRA means invention effectively filed before JRA and exception fails; (4) JRA limited to different activities/invention means exception does not apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These fact patterns illustrate the importance of effective filing dates, provisional priority chains, and the scope/timing of the JRA in determining eligibility for the exception (see Examples 1–4 in the text).

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission remains subject to rules of practice and may be refused in final-rejection status
rubrics_metrics.description: Filing an amendment or submission to invoke the JRA/common-ownership exception remains subject to the rules of practice (e.g., 37 CFR 1.116, 1.121, 1.312) and may be refused entry in certain procedural situations (for example, an amendment submitted in an application under final rejection).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an amendment is submitted under final rejection to overcome a rejection based on a U.S. patent qualifying under 102(a)(2), the examiner may refuse to enter the amendment if not properly accompanied by any needed terminal disclaimer or if procedural rules prevent entry.
